legal_principles.principle: The power of arrest should be sparingly drawn out and wielded only if necessary.
legal_principles.held: This weapon should not be used at the whim and fancy of the I.O. or be treated as a panacea for checking such offences.

legal_principles.principle: The attitude to arrest first and then proceed with the rest is despicable.
legal_principles.held: Mechanical, casual and hasty application of the power of arrest is counter-productive and negates the fundamental right enshrined in Art. 21.

legal_principles.principle: The need for caution in exercising the drastic power of arrest is emphasized.
legal_principles.held: The need to keep the doors for reconciliation open and to restore the family ties if possible has also been highlighted in many judgments and even in statutory provisions.

judgments.case_name: A.Pradeep vs R.Kavitha
judgments.facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties took place on 01.04.2001 at Reddiyarpalayam Police Station, Pondicherry. The appellant filed a petition under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to dissolve the marriage. The Family Court dismissed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking annulment to establish that the marriage was not valid due to coercion.
legal_principles.held: We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent. We have also gone through the pleadings, the evidence on record both documentary and oral recorded and impugned order passed by the Family Court.

legal_principles.principle: A party seeking annulment must establish the alleged fear and cessation of that fear before approaching the court.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court has concluded that the marriage between the appellant and the respondent cannot be annulled as the appellant has not established by way of evidence of the alleged fear and cessation of alleged fear before approaching the Court in a petition under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

outcome.final_order: The impugned order dated 18.03.2011 passed by the Family Court was set aside.

judgments.case_name: A. Premchand vs V. Padmapriya
judgments.facts_of_case: The husband and wife got married in 1987 but the marriage was not consummated. The wife's father sent a false horoscope to the husband seeking alliance for his daughter. The husband discovered the truth and the wife's family apologized for the fraud.

legal_principles.principle: Consent obtained prior to the date of marriage cannot be considered fraudulent if the correct information was disclosed.
legal_principles.held: In view of the specific pleadings in the counter affidavit, which has not been denied by way of filing a reply by the husband, as well as the oral evidence of the wife that the appellant was aware of the correct date of birth as 6-1-1961 prior to the date of marriage, i.e., on 8-3-87, it is not open to the appellant to contend that his consent was obtained fraudulently.
cited_cases: A. Premchand vs V. Padmapriya on 1 November, 1996

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging fraud to prove that consent was obtained by misrepresentation or concealment.
legal_principles.held: It is not open to the appellant to contend that his consent was obtained fraudulently.

outcome.final_order: The marriage was annulled by decree of nullity.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for nullity of marriage

judgments.case_name: A.R.Indira vs N.Kadappan
judgments.facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized in 1988. The wife left her matrimonial home in 1989 and did not return. The husband filed a petition for divorce in 2006 on grounds of cruelty and desertion.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove the grounds for divorce.
legal_principles.held: The respondent/husband cannot be permitted to make his submission on this ground [delay] for the first time only in this appeal.

legal_principles.principle: A party's condonation of the other party's cruelty does not necessarily mean that the divorce should be granted.
legal_principles.held: This would clearly show that he had condoned the cruelty and therefore, both the Courts below have erred in granting divorce on the ground of cruelty.

outcome.final_order: The order dated 12.04.2011 made by the trial court was set aside, and the fair and decreetal order dated 24.10.2007 was confirmed.
